about: Dr. Konstantin Frank Winery sits on the west shore of Keuka Lake, about six miles north of Hammondsport, on land its founder bought in 1958. Frank, born in Odessa in 1899, had managed vineyards in Soviet Georgia and believed European grapes could survive New York winters if properly grafted and protected. He was right, and the winery he opened in 1962 is now in its fourth generation of the Frank family, its wines poured for a British queen, American presidents and visiting heads of state.

Merlot is grown mostly on the family’s Seneca Lake vineyards, including the warm “Banana Belt” on the lake’s shores, with a smaller share from Keuka Lake’s shallow, shale-based soils. The winery’s method is consistent from year to year: the grapes are destemmed, cold-soaked for several days and fermented in open-top, temperature-controlled stainless steel with punchdowns and pumpovers, then aged about 16 months in French oak, roughly a fifth of it new.

The winery describes the 2022 as showing black cherry, cassis, vanilla and chocolate, with a thread of tobacco and silky tannins. Grown this far north, Merlot keeps more of its natural acidity than it does in warmer regions, so the wine stays medium-bodied and fresh rather than heavy, while the French oak adds the vanilla and spice notes that round out the dark fruit.
facts: Mostly Seneca Lake (Banana Belt), some Keuka Lake
Cold soak; open-top stainless steel fermentation with punchdowns and pumpovers
About 16 months in French oak, about 20% new (as in other vintages)
